blocks.html: “Closed for modification” = existing tested code should not be edited to add that new behavior.

blocks.html: How to check if the code follows OCP
blocks.text: How to check if the code follows OCP

blocks.html: Rule 1 — New Feature Addition Without Editing Existing Code
blocks.text: Rule 1 — New Feature Addition Without Editing Existing Code

blocks.html: It must be possible to add a new feature or variation without modifying existing tested code.
blocks.text: It must be possible to add a new feature or variation without modifying existing tested code.

blocks.html: Check: Simulate adding a new requirement. If it requires touching old business logic, OCP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Simulate adding a new requirement. If it requires touching old business logic, OCP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 2 — Polymorphic Extension
blocks.text: Rule 2 — Polymorphic Extension

blocks.html: Behavior variation must be achieved via interfaces, abstract classes, or similar mechanisms.
blocks.text: Behavior variation must be achieved via interfaces, abstract classes, or similar mechanisms.

blocks.html: Check: See if extending functionality involves creating new types or functions rather than editing old ones.
blocks.text: Check: See if extending functionality involves creating new types or functions rather than editing old ones.

blocks.html: Rule 3 — No Growing Conditional Chains
blocks.text: Rule 3 — No Growing Conditional Chains

blocks.html:
No need to modify an existing
switch
or
if/else
block to add new behavior.
blocks.text: No need to modify an existing switch or if/else block to add new behavior.

blocks.html: Check: If extending requires adding a new branch to an existing conditional statements, OCP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: If extending requires adding a new branch to an existing conditional statements, OCP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 4 — Stable Core Logic
blocks.text: Rule 4 — Stable Core Logic

blocks.html: Core processing logic should remain unchanged as new features are added.
blocks.text: Core processing logic should remain unchanged as new features are added.

blocks.html: Check: Review recent commits for feature additions. If core files keep changing for each new case, OCP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Review recent commits for feature additions. If core files keep changing for each new case, OCP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 5 — Dependency on Abstractions
blocks.text: Rule 5 — Dependency on Abstractions

blocks.html: The system should depend on general contracts (interfaces/abstract classes) rather than specific implementations.
blocks.text: The system should depend on general contracts (interfaces/abstract classes) rather than specific implementations.

blocks.html: Check: If the main logic depends directly on concrete classes, OCP risk is high.
blocks.text: Check: If the main logic depends directly on concrete classes, OCP risk is high.

blocks.html: Rule 6 — Isolated Testing for Extensions
blocks.text: Rule 6 — Isolated Testing for Extensions

blocks.html: New functionality should be testable independently without re-testing unrelated features.
blocks.text: New functionality should be testable independently without re-testing unrelated features.

blocks.html: Check: See if testing a new feature requires running the old feature’s tests due to shared code changes.
blocks.text: Check: See if testing a new feature requires running the old feature’s tests due to shared code changes.

blocks.html: Rule 7 — Minimal Change Surface
blocks.text: Rule 7 — Minimal Change Surface

blocks.html: The number of files modified for an extension should be small and limited to the new functionality.
blocks.text: The number of files modified for an extension should be small and limited to the new functionality.

blocks.html: Check: Count modified files for the last feature. If it includes unrelated files, OCP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Count modified files for the last feature. If it includes unrelated files, OCP is violated.
